text:
lodash is bumped to 4.17.21 (from 4.17.15), but the tests don't pass: 3 fail in `src/utils/date-utils.spec.js` ("formats DST boundary in America/New_York", "parses local midnight", "rolls over month end in local tz"). Whether lodash caused them is unverified.

The `git stash` rerun failed the same 3 tests, but it probably didn't undo the bump. Stash only reverts tracked files, and `node_modules` still held 4.17.21 during that run. This directory also isn't a git repo, so the stash and pop may have done nothing. Check that `package.json` and the lockfile still show 4.17.21.

The failing tests are all timezone-dependent, so a sandbox timezone mismatch is the likelier cause than lodash. That is an inference, not something I've confirmed.

To settle it, run `npm install lodash@4.17.15 && npm test`, which tests the old version for real. Then run `TZ=America/New_York npm test` on the new version. If the old version also fails and the TZ run passes, the failures are environmental and the bump is fine.
